editorial:
You get a bright, fast spy comedy where a smooth secret agent and a nerdy inventor clash, then learn to work together. Lance Sterling is all confidence and cool moves, while Walter Beckett is awkward but brilliant, building gadgets that avoid hurting people. Their opposite personalities make every scene lively, and the pigeon twist gives the story a silly, surprising energy that keeps kids and adults laughing all the way through.

The animation is colorful, the action scenes move quickly, and the voice cast brings charm to both heroes. The humor lands best when Lance struggles with bird life, though some jokes feel familiar and the villain is fairly standard. If you want a light family movie with heart, this is a fun pick for a weekend night.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Lance and Walter stop Killian from using a dangerous drone weapon, and Walter's cure turns Lance back from a pigeon into a human. Lance realizes Walter's non-lethal ideas can work, so he accepts him as a real partner instead of just a gadget maker. The movie ends with the two working together as a team, showing that kindness and teamwork can beat brute force.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves animated spy adventures and family-friendly action.
